LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD performs network requests in the global scope via command substitution, which will execute during sourcing of the file — exactly when `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` runs. Specifically, it uses `curl` to fetch data from `https://api.pcloud.com/getpublinkdownload` using a hardcoded API code. This request occurs unconditionally at the top level, meaning it will be triggered simply by parsing the PKGBUILD, before any build or prepare phase.

This is dangerous because it automatically contacts a remote server with a fixed token (`_api_code`) every time the PKGBUILD is sourced, potentially allowing the package maintainer or a compromised pcloud.com endpoint to log IPs, correlate downloads, or even exfiltrate limited system information via the request (e.g., through User-Agent or DNS lookups). While the payload is used to construct a download URL for the AppImage, the act of making an authenticated, automated network call during PKGBUILD parse time constitutes an unacceptable supply-chain risk.

Furthermore, the use of `curl | grep | cut | tr` to parse JSON is fragile and could be exploited if the API response is manipulated, although no direct code execution is evident from this snippet alone. Still, the automatic execution of `curl` with a secret-like token in the global scope violates secure packaging practices and makes this PKGBUILD unsafe to source without execution.
</details>

The PKGBUILD performs untrusted network operations during sourcing, specifically in the top-level scope. It runs `_api_response="$(curl -s "https://api.pcloud.com/getpublinkdownload?code=${_api_code}")"` to fetch data from a remote API using a hardcoded API key. While the intent may be to dynamically locate the AppImage, doing so via unsanitized command substitution during PKGBUILD parsing creates a supply-chain risk: an attacker controlling the API response could manipulate shell variables and potentially execute arbitrary code. Even if no code execution occurs, this behavior exfiltrates the user's IP address and potentially other metadata to pcloud.com during package preparation — without any user interaction or warning.

Such dynamic source resolution is not necessary for packaging and should be avoided in favor of static, auditable URLs.
</details>
